A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemInfo parsing work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.9 support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilingual parsing experiments, correlation analyses, optimization comparisons, and robustness and parser-agreement results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised parser-agreement values in Figure 13.

M1.justification: The appendix V-function pseudocode changes its loop from iterating over splits to iterating over spans of each length, a limited procedural correction. The main SemInfo scoring and training equations remain unchanged. New sampler listings document the existing recursive procedure, and Stepwise is renamed Action-V.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate constituency parsing on English PTB, Chinese CTB, and French/German SPMRL. The appendix retains the same paraphrasing-noise scenarios and constituent-type coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain the same in the benchmark tables, optimization comparisons, robustness tests, and agreement matrices. Action-V corresponds to the earlier Stepwise strategy; it is not an additional comparator.

E3.justification: The stated dataset splits, PCFG sizes, evaluation metrics, correlation-training budgets, and checkpoint analyses are retained. Explicitly describing punctuation-free training clarifies previously unspecified preprocessing rather than establishing a changed experiment. Figure 5 reuses examples already in Figure 8.

E4.justification: The parser-diversity diagnostic supporting potential ensembling is revised through changed agreement data in Figure 13. Optimization ablations, paraphrasing robustness tests, training-stage correlations, and constituent-type analyses otherwise remain. The expanded Figure 5 adds no new analysis beyond existing appendix examples.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-run means and standard deviations, two-tailed t-tests at p < 0.05, eight independently seeded models for correlation analysis, and Fisher-Z aggregation. No changed uncertainty-estimation practice or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5–7 retain their numerical results. Figure 13 changes agreement values: SemInfo-NPCFG versus SemInfo-SNPCFG changes from 80 to 75, and versus SemInfo-TNPCFG from 81 to 73. v3 also introduces a 5x speed summary in Section 4, while both appendices report model-specific 4x and 8x speedups. These are limited reporting changes, not benchmark accuracy gains.

T1.justification: Equation 4 removes the 1/|D| multiplier, and v3 omits the explicit assumptions that corpus sentences are equally probable and represent distinct semantics. Section 2 also changes the illustrated span-posterior potential from exp(P) to P. The operational score in Equation 10 and the span-posterior proof in Appendix A.2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a SemInfo objective, a bag-of-substrings estimator, TreeCRF-based PCFG training, stronger correlation with parsing accuracy, a reported average 7.85-point improvement, and state-of-the-art results in three languages. Rewording does not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a model-capacity explanation for NPCFG's weak Action-V result, referring to preliminary higher-capacity experiments. Appendix A.6 removes the earlier qualification that high agreement between independent runs might limit ensembling benefits, while retaining Figure 11.

D1.justification: v3 adds explicit TreeCRF/PCFG sampler pseudocode, an approximately $5 paraphrasing-cost statement, and clearer descriptions of punctuation preprocessing and bracket-form GPT predictions. Conversely, Appendix A.6 drops the explicit agreement-calculation definition and prediction-source details. Section 8 relocates the existing code-access information rather than announcing a new release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chia et al. (2023) and removes Blei et al. (2003) and Yang et al. (2018). Ensemble compatibility receives a main-text related-work paragraph, although that relationship was already discussed in v2's appendix. The central positioning against prior parsing approaches remains.

P1.justification: Substantial passages across the abstract, introduction, background, method, experimental discussion, and appendix are rewritten. Section 3 separates model definition, maximal-substring calculation, and SemInfo estimation; Appendix A.1 gains a dedicated V-function subsection. Reproducibility and acknowledgment sections are added, alongside terminology revisions.

P2.justification: The ICLR format substantially changes text width, typography, and figure/table sizing and placement. Figure 2 adds a bag-of-words comparison panel; Figure 5 displays two existing appendix examples; agreement heatmaps are reformatted, including Figure 11's fractional scale. These are extensive presentation changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: The reorganized explanation, expanded Figure 2, and clearer appendix algorithms make the method easier to understand and implement. These provide a modest overall gain while the central experimental evidence remains stable. Unexplained Figure 13 revisions and the loss of some Appendix A.6 reproducibility details temper the improvement.
